item.title: 3 Days To All Ireland Final For Cromane
item.description: Just three days remain until Cromane line out in the All-Ireland Final. They’re preparing to face the Leinster champions in the AIB Ladies All-Ireland Junior Club Football Championship decider. Cromane manager Anna Maria O'Donoghue says being involved with Kerry over recent seasons has helped give the team real confidence… Advertisement Sunday's final throws in at 2 o’clock at Parnell Park, where the Kerry and Munster champions will meet Muckalee of Kilkenny.

item.title: Ioane Gets First Start For Leinster
item.description: Reiko Ioane will make his first start for Leinster tomorrow when they travel to Leicester Tigers in the Champions Cup. Robbie Henshaw returns to the centre, James Lowe comes back from injury, and Harry Byrne starts at out-half alongside Jamison Gibson-Park. Sam Prendergast is listed among the replacements. item.title: Planning permission sought for 40 homes in Tralee
item.description: Planning is sought for 40 new homes on the outskirts of Tralee town. Tello Developments Ltd is applying for permission to construct the houses at Springmount, Ballyard. The company plans to build two storey semi-detached and terraced residential dwellings and is seeking a 10-year planning permission. item.title: Ireland South MEP says US proposals relating to tourists social media are concerning
item.description: An Ireland South MEP says proposals by the US that would see officials checking the social media history of tourists are concerning. These proposals suggest that visitors may have the last five years of their social media investigated by US authorities before they're allowed to enter the States. Fine Gael MEP Seán Kelly, who is from Kilcummin, says these proposals must be toned down and he feels they are impinging on the basic principles of freedom of expression. item.title: Kerry agricultural organisations welcome extension of nitrates derogation
item.description: Agricultural organisations in Kerry have welcomed the official extension of Ireland's nitrates derogation. The Nitrates Directive is an EU law which limits the amount of fertilizer and livestock manure that can be spread on land. The EU agreed on Tuesday to extend a derogation allowing Ireland use more than other bloc countries for the next three years. item.title: Former soldier to be sentenced next week for murder of Mid Kerry pensioner
item.description: A man found guilty of murdering his close friend in Mid Kerry will be sentenced next week. Thomas Carroll with an address at Brookway, Clonmel, Co Tipperary was found guilty of the murder of 84-year-old Paddy O'Mahony at Ballyreameen, near Castlemaine, on February 24th 2024. The 67-year-old accepted that he fired the gun, but denied the charge of murder.
